text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsg's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that the implementation of the agriculture, pension, health care, public administration and court reforms are the government's top legislative priorities this year. @

- The economic cabinet agreed on a privatisation concept for the state airline Malev, decided that the state shipping company Mahart will take delivery of three ocean liners as part payment of the Russian state debt and agreed to make HUF 500 million available in interest subsidies for development or export loans taken out by small and medium sized companies.

- A commission has been formed to examine the regulations on social insurance contribution introduced January 1, and present a report on whether it will be necessary to clarify the rules or possibly amend them. @

- Peter Simsa, vice-president of the health insurance authority, warned that the revenues of social insurance funds could drop by HUF 200-300 billion this year, due to the size of the present social insurance contributions.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs expressed disappointment after Switzerland handed over a list containing the names of 33 original owners or inheritors of sleeping accounts, as the total of the deposits on the list is less than estimated by Hungary. Peter Feldmajer, president of the Hungarian Jewish Communities, told Reuters that the 33 names form only a fraction of what he supposes to be the full figure. @

- As a result of the changes begun in the second half of last year, a slight economic boom is expected to take place in 1997, according to a joint study by the Economic Research Institute GKI and Postabank.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Premier Horn said in an interview with the Austrian paper Kurier that the Hungarian population is paying an exorbitant price to ensure that Hungary can join the EU at the earliest possible date. @
- A British analysis proposes that more civilians work in the Defence Ministry, and calls for greater transparency in the management of the military, deputy state secretary Jozsef Feher said.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will make a one-day visit to the Netherlands on Thursday.
- Former US Defence Secretary William Perry has been honoured by Hungary for his efforts to strengthen Euro-Atlantic integration and for promoting Hungarian-US military cooperation. @
- The carmakers Audi, Ford, Open and Suzuki are expected to together invest more than $1.5 billion into their Hungarian subsidiaries this year.
- Family doctors have reported 15,297 cases of severe influenza early this week against 7,200 cases last week.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said that the government is planning to reduce the rate of the crawling-peg devaluation of the forint sometime around April. @
- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin has warned that he advocates the simultaneous admission to NATO of countries belonging to the same geopolitical region.
- Eastern Sugar BV, comprising English company Tate & Lyle and the French firm Generale Sucriere has purchased a further 40 percent of the sugar factory Kabai Cukorgyar.
- Polgari Bank has been directed by a new management since January 21.
